title: Choose the look of your coaching dashboard
question: The roll assigned Tactics Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tactics Board
options.lineage: a coach's chalkboard in the film room; a whiteboard in light mode
options.thesis: Each game broken down like a coach reviewing tape: the play that cost you is drawn on the board.
materials: chalk strokes as the only drawing
options.viewport: Your games in a left rail; the coach's verdict on one reversed plate; win-chance chart and mistake list on the left; the tactics board (minimap) on the right with the selected mistake drawn as a play.
options.risk: Chalk can tip into costume; it stays a flat colour field with drawn strokes, never a photo of a blackboard.

raised.raise: State carried by line form as well as colour: your deaths are solid chalk ticks, teammates' dashed, enemies' hairline, so it reads without colour.
The board shows the model's own 24x24 movement grid as faint chalk lines, because that is literally how the model sees the map.
Every game clock sits right-aligned in one tabular column; lists never wrap their times.
Exactly one reversed plate per screen: the coach's verdict.
One geometry draws the board and names its areas: the same lane and jungle shapes the coach uses to say 'your safe-lane jungle'.

options.label: Game Review
options.lineage: chess engine analysis: evaluation bar and annotated move list
options.thesis: Your game annotated like an engine review: a win-chance bar and ?? on every blunder.
options.viewport: A full-height evaluation bar beside the event list, each death and fight annotated with a glyph; the minimap as the board on the right.
options.risk: The most familiar framing (chess sites ship exactly this review), so it can read as borrowed.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.thesis: A quiet neutral dashboard where every coaching sentence sits beside the moment that proves it.
options.viewport: Verdict and summary on top; each mistake as a row pairing the coach's sentence with its minimap snapshot and win-chance dip.
options.case: Holds product clarity; loses on identification: it could be any analytics product, nothing says Dota.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Events as hairline emission lines on one rail.
options.viewport: A single time rail with every event as a line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: Dota players don't identify with spectrograms, and one rail hides the map.
options.risk: Too abstract for a post-game check.
options.kept: State carried by line form, not only colour.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid as the layout.
options.viewport: Monumental grid-built numbers over small text.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a poster grid fights a dense working screen.
options.kept: The grid shown as part of the design (the model's real movement grid).

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Radiant and Dire as side A and side B.
options.viewport: A folded tracklist of the game's events.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nostalgic and unrelated to the game.
options.kept: Running times right-aligned tight against the margin.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides along the game.
options.case: Fuses poorly: raked slides cost readability on a chart-heavy screen.
options.kept: Exactly one reversed plate per screen.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Map areas as flat swelling colour lobes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful lobes clash with a serious review.
options.kept: One geometry drives the map, its labels and its state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark esports stat site, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Scoreboard header, stat tiles, then tabs of tables.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the stat sites you already use.
